answers.answer: No. In SCOPe 2.08, d1s9za_ (PDB 1S9Z, 'Amyloidogenic design') and d1hqja_ (PDB 1HQJ, 'Unnamed design') are not homologous, and SCOPe does not assert that they are, even though both sit in the same part of the hierarchy. Both domains belong to class k, 'Designed proteins'. Class k is one of the non-evolutionary classes in SCOP/SCOPe (together with h coiled coils, i low-resolution structures, and j peptides); the fold, superfamily and family nodes inside class k are organizational groupings of de novo designs by shared architecture (e.g. alpha-helical coiled-coil or hairpin designs), not statements of common ancestry. SCOPe's own documentation states that the hierarchy levels in these classes do not carry their usual evolutionary meaning, so co-membership of a class-k family does not imply homology the way a true family in classes a–g does. The two entries are independent laboratory designs: 1S9Z is the ccbeta peptide of Kammerer and colleagues (PNAS 2004), a short designed coiled-coil trimer built to switch into amyloid fibrils; 1HQJ is a separately conceived designed helical oligomer whose authors gave it no name, hence SCOP's 'Unnamed design' label. Neither has a natural evolutionary history, so there is no ancestor they could share; any sequence resemblance (heptad-repeat hydrophobic patterning) reflects shared design rules, not descent. Consequences: (1) no homology-based function transfer should be made between them, nor from either to natural proteins, even if they share a class-k fold/superfamily/family node; (2) structural similarity may make one a usable geometric template for the other, but that is template use by architecture only, not inference of homology; (3) the SCOPe 'family-specific' pair status that would be meaningful in classes a–g should not be treated as true for this pair, which is why it is a trap for automated evaluation that reads same-family membership as 'homologous'. No external evidence type (sequence profile hits, HMM scores, or structural alignment) could establish homology here, because homology presupposes descent that de novo designs lack; such evidence could only quantify design-level similarity. Caveat: I am reasoning from memory of the SCOP/SCOPe class-k organization and the two PDB entries, without consulting SCOPe 2.08 records, so the exact sunids/sccs of the two nodes are not stated.
